title: Silence the debug line
prompt:
Ciel's benchmark prints a debug line that nobody else should see.

In C++, // starts a comment that lasts to the end of the line, and /* ... */ can cover many lines. The compiler throws comments away.

Comment out the DEBUG line. Don't delete it. The program should print exactly:

Midnight lab session: Mon to Thu nights
Hopper Lab, Knuth Hall basement
hints: Put // in front of a line and the compiler skips it. The code stays in the file for later.
Change the DEBUG line to: // std::cout << "DEBUG: coffee level = 3%" << std::endl;
